title: Civic Skills Registry — SKILL.md frontmatter
description: The six fields of the Agent Skills specification, plus required civic.* metadata. Fields outside this set are quarantined into metadata by validator/src/rules.ts rather than rejected, so that skills using vendor extensions still validate.

name.description: Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens. Must match the parent directory name.

description.description: How an agent decides to invoke this skill. Must describe actual behavior, not aspiration. A description broader than the behavior is a security finding, not a style issue.

license.description: Optional in the Agent Skills spec; required here. SPDX identifier by convention — the spec does not constrain this field, so it is machine-present but not machine-verifiable. License applicability is a human review step.

compatibility.description: Network, credential, and platform requirements, stated plainly.

allowed-tools.description: Least privilege. This grant applies without a permission prompt and is not gated by workspace trust. Marked EXPERIMENTAL in the Agent Skills spec — re-verify semantics before relying on it. Wildcard Bash grants are rejected by scripts/scan.py at layer L2.

metadata.description: String map, per the Agent Skills spec. Registry fields are namespaced civic.* so they cannot collide with vendor extensions.

allOf.$comment: Saying a team or an organization uses this is a claim about them, and an unnamed organization is a claim nobody can check. civic.deployed-in is no longer required alongside it (#67): the checkable part is the name, and where the organization operates is often implied by civic.jurisdiction.
civic.deployment: none says the skill has never been used, so it cannot also name where it was used.

A generalized skill has had its jurisdiction specifics lifted out into a context an adopter fills in, so it names no place. One direction only: a skill that names no place was not necessarily generalized from anything.
A commit on its own names a point in a history nobody can find.
civic.scope: any says the skill works at every level of government, so it is not tied to a particular place.

civic.category.$comment: The permitted values live in registry/categories.yml and are enforced at runtime by validator/src/rules.ts, so the vocabulary has exactly one source of truth. x-vocabulary names the published artifact a program should read them from.

civic.category-secondary.$comment: Optional second category, from the same vocabulary as civic.category. Two explicit fields rather than a list because metadata values are strings per the Agent Skills spec, and because the cap of two is then structural. Must differ from civic.category; enforced by validator/src/rules.ts, which JSON Schema cannot express.
civic.category-secondary.description: Optional. The other axis this skill sits on — the vocabulary mixes function inside the organization with public service delivered, and a skill often belongs to one of each. civic.category is the primary and is what a plugin manifest carries.

civic.scope.description: What kind of government body the skill is written for. Replaces the old civic.jurisdiction enum, which conflated level of government, country-ness and whether any of it applied — and which every listing answered 'generic'. Country-neutral, because civic.jurisdiction now carries the country: 'regional' covers a state, province, prefecture, canton or region, and 'municipal' covers a city, county or town. 'any' is explicit rather than implied by omission, because an omitted scope cannot be told apart from an unanswered one.

civic.scope-secondary.description: Optional second level, for a skill that genuinely serves two. Must differ from civic.scope, and cannot be paired with 'any', which already means every level. Enforced by validator/src/rules.ts.

civic.jurisdiction.description: Optional. The specific place the skill is written for: ISO 3166 country, optional subdivision, optional locality. e.g. 'US-VT', 'US-MA / Boston', 'CA-ON / Toronto'. Set only when the skill is tied to one place — a skill that is not simply omits it. Distinct from civic.deployed-in, which is where the organization that used it operates; a generalized skill has no jurisdiction and may still have been deployed somewhere. Same shape as that field because both name a place.

civic.data-sensitivity.description: What the skill is expected to touch. 'protected' covers health, benefits, immigration, criminal justice, and anything else under a statutory regime.

civic.human-review.description: Whether output affects a person's rights, benefits, or legal standing. Anything other than 'none' must also be stated in the skill's own output, not only here.

civic.use-when.description: Optional. The concrete situations where this skill earns its place. Plain text, never markdown — the site renders it on the landing page, which publishes no submitter-authored markup.

civic.avoid-when.description: Optional. Where the skill falls down and what it should not be pointed at. The higher-value half of the pair — nobody but the author can supply it — so the submission form pushes for it even though it stays optional. Plain text, never markdown.

civic.maintainer.description: Organization or individual accountable for the skill.

civic.affiliation.description: Affiliation of the party named in civic.maintainer. Self-reported; verification is a reviewer step recorded in registry/reviewed.yml, never here.

civic.deployment.description: Widest scope at which this skill has actually been used. 'none' means it has not been used in production anywhere, which is an honest and acceptable answer.

civic.deployed-at.description: The organization where it was used. Required when civic.deployment is 'team' or 'organization' — those are claims about an organization, and an unnamed one cannot be checked. Not required for 'personal', which asserts nothing about an organization; forbidden for 'none'.

civic.deployed-in.description: Where that organization operates: ISO 3166 country, optional subdivision, optional locality. e.g. 'US-MA / Boston', 'GB', 'CA-ON / Toronto'. Required alongside civic.deployed-at, optional for 'personal', forbidden for 'none'.

civic.deployed-since.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM. Optional. Duration of real use is the part of a deployment claim that carries the most weight.

civic.localization.description: Where the skill sits on the jurisdiction axis. 'localized' carries one jurisdiction's specifics; 'generalized' has had them lifted out into a context an adopter fills in. Optional — omit it when the skill has no jurisdiction-specific content either way. See docs/LOCALIZATION.md.

civic.source-repo.description: Where an imported copy came from, as owner/repository. Optional; a skill written here has no upstream. The registry always holds the content — this records the origin so a reader can look, and nothing in the build resolves it. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

civic.source-commit.description: The upstream commit the copy was taken from. Full 40-character SHA; a short one stops being unique as a repository grows. Requires civic.source-repo.

version.description: Optional. The author's own claim about which version of the skill this is: MAJOR.MINOR, optionally MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Unprefixed because the Agent Skills specification's own example writes metadata.version and a version is not civic-specific. Not validated beyond the shape — monotonicity is unenforceable, since nothing can know the previous value. A claim, not a fact: the registry derives first_seen, last_changed and commits from git, and publishes those flatly. Neither may influence tier or order the catalogue.
